title: 03 Quietfield: newsletter-led dark footer with a glowing horizon
strengths: Type is quiet: Sora 300 for the headline, three small link columns tucked top-right, a tiny legal row
Copy has a human line: 'Read by 31,000 researchers and a few very patient parents' and 'No tracking pixels. Leave with one click.'
slop_signals: A planet's edge glowing violet, magenta and amber over a starfield: the gradient-horizon glow that AI landing pages default to, with no link to interpretability research
Centred headline where the second line is bold ('before it becomes a paper.'): the bold-phrase trick
Pill email field with the white pill button inside it, centred, with a note underneath: the standard newsletter block
'LATEST' amber chip inside a rounded pill with the post title: a badge inside a badge
Label flanked by dashes ('— DISPATCH NO. 41 · OCTOBER 2026 —') above the headline
Nothing of the lab's actual work appears; the only picture is atmosphere
fixes: Remove the planet and the starfield; let the ground be plain near-black
Make the picture the lab's work: a feature-activation figure, an attention map or a sparse-feature plot drawn in one colour, as the Daylight reference uses grain and light rather than a scene
Left-align the newsletter block with the link columns beside it, as Spade does; input and button as separate plain controls
Drop the 'LATEST' chip; list the latest letter as the first link under Research

references.what: Warm light bleeds in from the edges with heavy grain and no horizon; pill field with the button inside; the glow is texture, not a scene
Dark footer with mono labels, link columns left and the newsletter top-right; no art at all and it holds
The centred-newsletter-on-dark-gradient pattern ours resembles most; already a cliché in 2023
'Enter your email' set as the headline inside a card, links below; a newsletter-led footer with an idea instead of a glow
